config.title: Offline Order Queue

intro.title: Offline Order Queue
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build an offline mutation queue for a mobile app, which allows users to perform actions like creating or updating data even when they have no internet connection. You will learn how to store these pending actions locally on the device using Ionic Storage, a key-value storage system. The core concept involves creating a service that queues data operations and later syncs them to a server when the network is restored. This ensures your app remains functional and provides a smooth user experience in offline scenarios.
intro.usecase: The offline mutation queue pattern is essential in mobile apps where network connectivity is unreliable, such as field service applications, delivery tracking systems, or remote data collection tools. For example, a delivery driver's app needs to record package scans and delivery confirmations even when in elevator shafts or rural areas with poor signal, queueing these mutations locally until connectivity is restored. Similarly, a field technician completing work orders in a manufacturing plant can submit inspection forms and photos offline, with all changes synchronized automatically when back online. This ensures data integrity and seamless user experience in critical mobile workflows where interruptions are common.

objectives: Define a mutation queue service using Angular's dependency injection system.
Construct an interface to represent mutation objects with required properties.
Implement a method to add new mutations to the queue with timestamp generation.
Apply array iteration to process pending mutations in the queue.
Use Capacitor's Network API to detect online/offline connectivity status.
Execute conditional statements to control when mutations should be queued versus sent.
Implement a retry mechanism to handle failed mutation submissions.
Store mutation data in Ionic Storage for persistence across app restarts.
Retrieve stored mutations from Ionic Storage when the app initializes.
Modify the mutation queue to remove successfully processed items.
Invoke the mutation processing method when network connectivity is restored.
Construct error handling to manage mutation failures and queue state.

steps.title: Create the main component structure
steps.instruction: Create a standalone Angular component class named 'OfflineQueuePage' with the @Component decorator. Set standalone: true and use an empty template for now.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator from '@angular/core' to define your component. Remember to export the class so it can be used elsewhere.
steps.expectedOutcome: A basic Angular component structure is created with the correct decorator configuration, ready for adding offline queue functionality.
successCriteria: Component must be named 'OfflineQueuePage', have @Component decorator with standalone: true, and an empty template string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the main component structure. This gives us a foundation to build our offline mutation queue functionality.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you have: 1) The @Component decorator, 2) standalone: true, 3) an empty template string, and 4) the component is named 'OfflineQueuePage'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component structure isn't quite right. Remember to use @Component decorator with standalone: true and an empty template. Check the example for the correct syntax.

steps.title: Define the Mutation interface
steps.instruction: Inside your component file, define a TypeScript interface called 'Mutation' with properties: id (string), type (string), payload (any), and timestamp (number).
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions with type annotations.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a properly typed Mutation interface that will be used to structure mutation objects in the offline queue.
successCriteria: The interface must be named 'Mutation' and include all four required properties with correct TypeScript types.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the Mutation interface with all required properties. This interface will serve as the blueprint for mutation objects in our offline queue.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the Mutation interface is missing some required properties or has incorrect types. Make sure to include: id (string), type (string), payload (any), and timestamp (number).
steps.feedbackWrong: The Mutation interface is not properly defined. You need to create an interface named 'Mutation' with the specified properties and types.

steps.hint: Add a property declaration in the component class. Use the type annotation ': Mutation[]' and set it equal to an empty array '[]'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a 'mutations' property ready to store pending mutation objects.
successCriteria: The component class contains a property declaration 'mutations' with type 'Mutation[]' initialized to an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the main data structure to store pending mutations. The 'mutations' array is now ready to hold mutation objects while the app is offline.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check: Did you declare the property with the correct type 'Mutation[]'? Did you initialize it as an empty array?
steps.feedbackWrong: The 'mutations' property is not correctly declared. Make sure you add a property inside the component class with the name 'mutations', type 'Mutation[]', and initialize it as an empty array.

steps.title: Initialize the online status state
steps.instruction: Inside the OfflineMutationQueueComponent class, declare a boolean property named 'isOnline' and initialize it to 'true'.
steps.hint: Add a property declaration with type annotation and initial value in the component class.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a boolean property 'isOnline' initialized to true, ready to track network connectivity.
successCriteria: The component class contains a property named 'isOnline' with type 'boolean' and initial value 'true'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully declared the isOnline property to track network connectivity.

steps.feedbackWrong: The isOnline property wasn't properly declared. Make sure to add 'isOnline: boolean = true;' inside the component class.

steps.title: Create the addMutation handler
steps.instruction: Inside the OfflineMutationQueueComponent class, create a method named addMutation that takes two parameters: type (string) and payload (any). The method should create a new mutation object with these properties plus an id (use Date.now() for simplicity) and a status of 'pending',
steps.hint: Remember to use the Mutation interface type for the new object. The method should have a void return type.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have an addMutation method that can be called to add new mutations to the queue with proper structure.
successCriteria: The method should be defined inside the class, take two parameters (type: string, payload: any), create a mutation object with id, type, payload, and status properties, and push it to the mutations array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the addMutation handler. This method will allow you to queue mutations when the app is offline.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your method: 1) Takes two parameters (type and payload), 2) Creates a complete mutation object with all required properties, 3) Pushes it to the mutations array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The addMutation method isn't quite right. Make sure you're creating a method inside the class that adds a properly structured mutation object to the mutations array.

steps.title: Create the processQueue handler
steps.instruction: Inside the OfflineMutationQueueComponent class, create a method named processQueue that checks if isOnline is true and clears the mutations array when it is.
steps.hint: Define a method with no parameters. Use an if statement to check the isOnline property. If true, set the mutations array to an empty array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a processQueue method that simulates processing the mutation queue by clearing it when online.
successCriteria: The processQueue method is defined, checks isOnline, and clears the mutations array when online.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the processQueue handler. This method will simulate processing pending mutations when the app is online.

steps.instruction: Inside the OfflineMutationQueueComponent class, create a method named toggleOnlineStatus that flips the boolean value of the isOnline property.
steps.hint: You can toggle the boolean by setting isOnline to its opposite value using the logical NOT operator (!).
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a toggleOnlineStatus method that can be called to simulate network connectivity changes by toggling the isOnline property between true and false.
successCriteria: Method is inside the component class
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the toggleOnlineStatus method. This will allow you to simulate network connectivity changes by flipping the isOnline boolean value.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the toggleOnlineStatus method needs to properly toggle the isOnline property. Make sure you're using the logical NOT operator (!) to flip the boolean value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggleOnlineStatus method is not correctly implemented. You need to create a method that toggles the isOnline property between true and false using the logical NOT operator (!).

steps.title: Add control buttons with click handlers
steps.instruction: Inside the component's template, add three IonButton elements: one with text 'Add Mutation' that calls the addMutation method when clicked, one with text 'Process Queue' that calls the processQueue method, and one with text 'Toggle Online Status' that calls the toggleOnlineStatus method.
steps.hint: Use the (click) event binding to connect each button to its corresponding method. The buttons should be placed within the template string.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of adding Ionic buttons with click handlers
<ion-button (click)="addItem()">Add Item</ion-button>
<ion-button (click)="processItems()">Process Items</ion-button>
<ion-button (click)="toggleStatus()">Toggle Status</ion-button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will contain three interactive buttons that trigger the mutation queue operations when clicked.
successCriteria: The template must include three IonButton elements with (click) event bindings to the correct methods: addMutation, processQueue, and toggleOnlineStatus.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the control buttons with their click handlers. Now users can interact with the mutation queue through these buttons.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some buttons, but check that all three are present with the correct (click) event bindings: 'Add Mutation' should call addMutation(), 'Process Queue' should call processQueue(), and 'Toggle Online Status' should call toggleOnlineStatus().
steps.feedbackWrong: The buttons aren't properly configured. Make sure you add three IonButton elements inside the template, each with the correct text and (click) event binding to the corresponding method.

steps.title: Display online status indicator
steps.instruction: In the component template, add a visual indicator that shows the current online status using the existing 'isOnline' state. Use Ionic components like IonBadge or IonChip with conditional styling.
steps.hint: You can use an IonBadge with color='success' when online and color='danger' when offline. Bind the color and text to the 'isOnline' property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will display a visual indicator (like a colored badge) that shows 'Online' when isOnline is true and 'Offline' when false, with appropriate color coding.
successCriteria: The template should contain an Ionic component (like IonBadge) that displays the current online status with conditional styling based on the 'isOnline' property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a visual indicator that clearly shows the network connectivity state. The badge changes color and text based on the isOnline property, providing immediate visual feedback.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a status indicator, but it might not be properly bound to the 'isOnline' property or missing conditional styling. Make sure the badge's color and text change dynamically based on the isOnline value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The status indicator is missing or doesn't properly reflect the online status. Check that you're using an Ionic component with property binding to display 'Online'/'Offline' text and appropriate colors based on the isOnline state.
